structs.name: TES3::AnimationData
structs.note: Xbox verified offsets: groups +0x38, semantic next-key indices +0x3C, flags +0x54, layer times +0x58, sequence pointer triples +0x2C4 and selected sequence indices +0x308. update 0x000CEFB0 skips setting upper/arm sequence offsets when flags are 0xFFFF; held playback must set them explicitly. Key time tables are semantic slots, including unused zeros and nonchronological entries.

structs.name: NI::Sequence
structs.note: Xbox time offset +0x54 verified in AnimationData::update 0x000CEFB0: upper/arm layer time minus lower-body time.

structs.name: TES3::MobileActor
structs.note: Xbox matches the PC layout at the offsets tested: attributes (+0x254, Statistic {vtable, base, current} each), health, magicka and fatigue current (+0x2BC, +0x2C8, +0x2E0), animationController (+0x244), animStateAttack (byte +0xDD: 5/6/7 light/medium/heavy follow-through), physicalAttackType (byte +0xE0: 1/2/3 slash/chop/thrust), activeEffects (+0x1C4; deque head +4, count +8).

fields.name: animStateAttack
fields.provenance: Xbox swingAnimationStateMachine 0x0016D710 and first-person held-punch trace: states 5/6/7 light/medium/heavy follow-through

structs.name: TES3::MobileNPC
structs.note: Xbox matches the PC at skills (+0x3B0, 27 SkillStatistic of 0x10; type +0xC is major, minor or misc, not the skill index).

structs.name: TES3::MobilePlayer
structs.note: Xbox matches the PC at clawMultiplier (+0x5AC), skillProgress (+0x5F4), firstPersonReference (+0x660), birthsign (+0x670) and lastPositionOfFogOfWarUpdate (+0x67C). restWaitPosition (+0x5D8) holds stale bytes until the player rests. Writing birthsign (from NonDynamicData::findBirthsign) is what the save's PCDT BNAM follows (xemu identity-a1).

structs.name: TES3::NPCInstance
structs.note: Xbox matches the PC at baseNPC (+0x6C); the player's reference (+0x28) is one, and its baseNPC's name (TES3::NPC +0x70) is the character's name.

structs.name: TES3::NPC
structs.note: Xbox matches the PC at name (+0x70), level (+0x7C, short; SetLevel on the player writes it), spellList (+0xC4) and aiConfig (+0xE0: fight +2, alarm +4; an Imperial Guard reads fight 30). SpellList's IteratedList head is at NPC +0xD0; each node has next at +4 and a TES3::Spell* at +8. The links table (+0x78) can be null after loading a player; when present it holds race, class, faction, head and hair ids, each a 32-byte buffer, which NPC::setClass writes and the save's RNAM/CNAM/BNAM/KNAM follow together with race (+0xB0), class (+0xB4), head (+0xBC) and hair (+0xC0) (xemu identity-a1, rebuild-c2).

fields.name: spellList
fields.provenance: xemu spells-a1/spells-b1: walking the player NPC's list found calm humanoid; AddSpell and RemoveSpell changed the list

structs.name: TES3::Clothing
structs.note: 0x10 shorter than the PC by +0x44: the 7 wearable parts (part index byte, -1 unused; male, female BodyPart*) start at +0x44 (PC +0x54) and the slot is the byte at +0x98 (PC +0xA8). Clothing::setupBodyParts 0x000EF430; xemu beast-a9 read common_shoes_01's feet parts there.

structs.name: TES3::Armor
structs.note: The 7 wearable parts start at +0x44 (PC +0x54), as on Clothing; Armor::setupBodyParts 0x000F1E80 walks them from there.

structs.name: TES3::Race
structs.note: Matches the PC at id (+0x10) and flags (+0xD8: 1 playable, 2 beast; xemu beast-a4 read 3 for Khajiit).

structs.name: TES3::Class
structs.note: Matches the PC: id[32] +0x10, name[32] +0x30, attributes[2] +0x50, specialization +0x58, skills[10] +0x5C, playable +0x84, description +0x8C. MenuCreateClass::create allocates 0x94 bytes for chargen's NEWCLASSID_CHARGEN (xemu identity-a2 made one the same way and the save wrote it).

structs.name: TES3::Dialogue
structs.note: 0x20 bytes on the Xbox (0x30 on the PC): the INFOs are an intrusive chain from a head pointer, not an inline list, so journalIndex sits at +0x1C. Retail has 2,884 dialogues, 758 of them journals (type 4).

fields.name: info
fields.provenance: head of the chain linked through DialogueInfo +0x1C: appendInfo 0x000FF680 and the by-name lookup 0x000FE0F0 walk it

fields.name: journalIndex
fields.provenance: xemu peek: 10 for A1_1_FindSpymaster after Journal A1_1_FindSpymaster 10

structs.name: TES3::DialogueInfo
structs.note: Same size as the PC, but DATA is packed into +0x14..+0x1B so +0x1C can link the topic's chain. The Xbox master stores DATA in that 8-byte form; a 12-byte PC DATA is repacked on load (0x000FE830). +0x20 conditions and +0x24 file offset match the PC.

fields.name: disposition
fields.provenance: INFO load 0x000FE830; journal index for journal topics

fields.name: conditions
fields.provenance: INFO copy 0x000FF230 walks it as the PC copy 0x004AFF10 does

fields.name: espFileOffset
fields.provenance: INFO copy 0x000FF230 and the PC copy 0x004AFF10 both carry it

structs.name: TES3::NonDynamicData
structs.note: 12 bytes longer than the PC at or before +0x44; the record lists and the cells list sit 0xC past their PC offsets. PC fields are left out until placed.

fields.name: classes
fields.provenance: PC +0x24; MenuCreateClass::onOk appends chargen's class to it

fields.name: globals
fields.provenance: PC +0x38, at the same 0xC shift as its neighbours

fields.name: dialogues
fields.provenance: PC +0x3C; xemu walk: 2,884 objects tagged DIAL

fields.name: cells
fields.provenance: PC +0xB264; ref-index and the multiplayer cell list

structs.name: TES3::MagicSourceInstance
structs.note: Xbox allocation is 0x128; no PC MCP original-target field. The eight 0x10-byte effect maps begin at +0x1C; each node has key +0, inline MagicEffectInstance +4, next +0x3C. Source combo +0xA0, serial +0xA8, corprus hours +0xAC, state +0xB4, caster +0xB8, casting item +0xBC and item data +0xC0 match PC. Verified against activateSpell, process, SpellEffectEvent and the save loader.

structs.name: TES3::MagicEffectInstance
structs.note: Xbox matches all 0x38 bytes of the PC layout: target +0, resistance +4, rolled magnitude +8, elapsed +0xC, cumulative magnitude +0x10, state +0x14, visual +0x18, created data +0x1C/+0x20 and last-used stacks +0x24..+0x34. The last seven pointers are rebuilt by callbacks, never serialized.

structs.name: TES3::ActiveMagicEffect
structs.note: Xbox matches the 0x10-byte PC entry: serial +0, effect index +4, effect id +6, harmful +8, illegal +9, duration +0xA, magnitude +0xC, skill/attribute +0xE. Padding +5 and +0xF is uninitialized and must not enter snapshot comparisons.

structs.name: TES3::Alchemy
structs.note: Xbox allocation is 0x110; fields after the common object header are 0x10 below PC. Constructor 0x000FC650 and getSourceEffects 0x000E7460 verify the layout.

structs.name: TES3::WorldController
structs.note: 4 bytes shorter than the PC somewhere in 0x70..0xA4: the clock globals, CharGenState and menu mode sit 4 below their PC offsets. PC fields from 0x70 on are left out until placed.

fields.name: gvarGameHour
fields.provenance: PC order at -4; 0xA4..0xB8 read as the clock globals by the multiplayer clock

fields.name: flagMenuMode
fields.provenance: menu pause: two jne skip the world while set

structs.name: TES3::UI::Element
structs.note: 8 bytes longer than the PC before 0x7D: the flags and the colour sit 8 above their PC offsets. Laying out the element above the top-level menus lays out every menu, and the HUD loses its place.

fields.name: visible
fields.provenance: ui::navigate 0x001B1050 skips menus with it clear; PC 0x75

fields.name: flagColourChanged
fields.provenance: a label's new colour shows only once it is set (Join server rows); PC 0x77
